core.subtitle: Complete workflow
core.title: How to analyze viral Xiaohongshu posts from discovery to new topic ideas
core.description: Viral post analysis is more than sorting by likes. Narrow the sample, preserve the original content, build a reviewable report, and decide which methods deserve a place in your own workflow.

items.title: 1. Search your niche for recent high-engagement posts
items.description: Search Xiaohongshu for a niche, product, or concrete problem. Use recency plus likes, saves, or comments to narrow the results, then set an engagement threshold before collecting candidates.

image.alt: Xiaohongshu search results filtered by recency and engagement before MediaClaw collects candidate posts

items.title: 2. Use low-follower filters to reduce creator-size bias
items.description: Set a follower ceiling to find smaller creators whose individual posts performed unusually well. Tune the threshold to your niche: these results are research candidates, not proof that a format will repeat.

image.alt: MediaClaw follower ceiling used to find low-follower, high-engagement Xiaohongshu posts

items.title: 3. Start a single-post breakdown from your research library
items.description: Choose a post worth studying. Image posts can combine captions, covers, and text extracted from images; video posts can add a transcript; public comments can be included when you need audience evidence.

image.alt: MediaClaw AI workspace with Xiaohongshu posts ready for single-post analysis

items.title: 4. Review the evidence and choose the next step
items.description: The report connects the core takeaway, title and cover, content structure, visual evidence, public feedback, and follow-up topic ideas. Reopen the source to verify the context, then save an idea or begin drafting.

image.alt: MediaClaw Xiaohongshu post breakdown with source evidence and analysis conclusions

report.subtitle: Single-post report
report.title: What should a Xiaohongshu viral post analysis examine?
report.description: A useful report must point back to the original post and public engagement evidence. Generic conclusions such as “strong emotion” or “an attractive title” are not enough.

items.title: Title, cover, and first screen
items.description: Identify the audience, situation, benefit, tension, or curiosity in the title; see how the cover adds information; then check whether the opening fulfills the promise that earned the click.

image.alt: Title, cover, and opening analysis in a Xiaohongshu post breakdown

items.title: Body or transcript structure and information flow
items.description: For image posts, follow body sections and text embedded in images; for video posts, follow the timed voiceover structure. Expand the full source text to check whether each conclusion is supported by the original content.

image.alt: Expanded source transcript in a MediaClaw Xiaohongshu breakdown for checking structure against the original voiceover

items.title: Public feedback and unanswered questions
items.description: Separate resonance, questions, objections, additions, and action intent, then expand the original comments included in the analysis to verify what readers actually responded to and which needs remain open.

image.alt: Expanded source comments in a MediaClaw Xiaohongshu breakdown for checking comment signals against public evidence

items.title: New topics based on the underlying method
items.description: Develop ideas by going deeper, changing the situation, or transferring the expression method. State what is retained and what changes so the result is not a close rewrite of the source.

scenarios.title: When is Xiaohongshu viral post analysis useful?

items.title: Find attainable examples for a new account
items.description: Study posts from creators near your scale that clearly outperformed, reducing the execution gap created by copying only top accounts.

items.title: Review content methods as a team
items.description: Discuss the source post, analysis, and comment evidence together instead of relying on screenshots, memory, or a vague claim that something went viral.

items.title: Expand one post into a topic series
items.description: Keep a proven expression method while changing the audience, problem, situation, and evidence to create genuinely new directions.

boundaries.subtitle: Analysis limits
boundaries.title: What Xiaohongshu viral post analysis cannot prove
boundaries.description: Public data and structured analysis improve judgment, but they cannot prove platform-algorithm causality or guarantee the same outcome when a method is reused.

items.title: High engagement is not the same as reproducibility
items.description: Account authority, paid promotion, trends, creator experience, and timing can all affect results. Separate content methods from external conditions.

items.title: Conclusions must remain traceable
items.description: Claims about titles, structure, visuals, and comments should point back to the source post and public evidence. Label inferences that cannot be verified.

items.title: Research public content only
items.description: MediaClaw does not provide platform-internal data, private-account information, or undisclosed audience profiles. Follow platform rules and applicable law.

items.question: Is Xiaohongshu viral post analysis based only on likes?
items.answer: No. Likes are one public signal. Review publish date, saves, comments, creator size, topic, and source structure as well. Filters narrow the sample but do not replace manual verification.

items.question: What is a low-follower viral post on Xiaohongshu?
items.answer: It generally means a post from a smaller creator that earned unusually strong public engagement relative to the account or comparable posts. Thresholds differ by niche, so MediaClaw lets you set your own follower ceiling and engagement floor.

items.question: Can MediaClaw analyze text inside Xiaohongshu images?
items.answer: Yes. After extracting text from the cover and images of a collected post, that text can be reviewed, exported, and used as evidence in the later breakdown.

items.question: Can video posts be analyzed too?
items.answer: Yes. Add a transcript first, then examine the title, opening, content structure, pacing, visuals, and public feedback in a single-post report.

items.question: Does a breakdown generate a close rewrite of the original post?
items.answer: The analysis first produces methods, evidence, and distinct follow-up topics. After choosing a direction, add your own examples, perspective, and constraints rather than copying the source.

items.question: Why should I still reopen the original post?
items.answer: A report organizes evidence but cannot replace the source context, creator conditions, trend background, or comment atmosphere. Source links keep important conclusions reviewable.
